note: T4-L1 (GPT review 7, finding 2; T4 review R1 S1; SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 4.6): what a /resolve's answer holds after its pass (the profile, the candidates, the selection, the JSON tree and its text) is priced per pair, before it is built, against --resolve-max-discover-memory-mb (1,024 MiB by default, 1 on the recording server so that the sample stays short; 0 = none, the bound of the pass too). An answer priced past it is refused 400, nothing partial sent. The work ran, so this is a refusal, not a stop: a part of an answer is not the answer of a prefix. The part in parentheses names what passed the bound: profile, candidates, selection or answer. On a single-graph server the body is {error, code: "resolve_answer_too_large", max_memory_mb}, written in this order (error first): for this request {"error":"resolve: the answer would hold more than --resolve-max-discover-memory-mb 1 MiB (answer): nothing partial is sent; ask for run_format \"rle\", a larger min_block_kmers, fewer labels or seeds, or a shorter sequence","code":"resolve_answer_too_large","max_memory_mb":1}. The request_id is freed with it (GET /requests/svc-res-t4-39s then answered 404, and the same id runs again), as for every 400 that only the work can find (SPEC-multigraph-envelope.md section 5). On a multi-graph server, as here, that pair is a refused entry of a 200 envelope, refusal.http_status 400 and the members in the server's byte order (code, error, http_status, max_memory_mb); the other pairs are answered. The request is retained like any answered one: GET /requests/svc-res-t4-39 states it ended, reason answered, bact_other refused (its usage memory_bytes 0), and the same id gets 409. work.memory_bytes sums the answered entries only. The same request is refused the same way, so a client treats the code as final and changes the request: run_format "rle" writes a label's runs as one string, a few bytes a run against about 350 B as intervals. A real run on fixture pairs the binary built (bact_other: 40 records of a 2,000 bp query with a SNP every 32 bp, 62 runs of one k-mer each; bact_pseudomonadota: 3 records the query does not touch), each entry tagged with its sample pair and identity. The run was on macOS: timing.page_faults, stated where the platform reads it per thread (Linux), is absent, never 0.
